articleTitle: Generating Sketch Faces from Text Descriptions: Dataset and Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: Sketching, as a form of painting, is widely used to pursue fugitives. The main method of modern criminal investigation sketching is for artists to sketch suspects' faces based on witness descriptions. However, to ensure that the sketches match the witness descriptions, the artists must possess both professional expertise and a substantial reservoir of experience. The process is inherently time-consuming. As a consequence of developments in the field of generative adversarial networks, it is possible to quickly generate corresponding sketch face images from text descriptions. However, this research is challenging due to two facts: first, there is no available dataset of face attribute text to sketches; second, due to the abstractness and simplicity of sketch images, it is difficult to synthesize high-quality face sketches. In this study, our contributions are twofold: 1) We propose a novel text-to-sketch face network, MDPGAN. 2) We build a comprehensive dataset, CelebASketch-HQ, which contains high-quality face sketch images, each accompanied by ten corresponding text descriptions. Finally, experimental evidence substantiates the efficacy of our approach.

articleTitle: Error Analysis and Reduction in 3D Reconstruction Based on Structured Light
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: In the process of structured light 3D reconstruction, the nonlinear response of projection equipment will greatly affect the accuracy of reconstruction. This paper introduces the reconstruction principle and process steps of n-step phase shift method with, complementary Gray code in, monocular inverse camera method, and analyzes the influence of phase shift error and phase error on the reconstruction results under different phase shift steps. In order to solve the contradiction between speed and accuracy of 3D reconstruction, this paper proposes to use multi-layer neural network and gray neighborhood information to solve the wrapped phase. Experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively compensate the reconstruction error, and can achieve a reconstruction accuracy of uncompensated 24 steps of phase shift by a 4 steps of phase shift, which can meet the needs of speed and accuracy of dynamic 3D reconstruction.

articleTitle: Edge Detection and Quantitative Analysis Based on Binary Mathematical Morphology and Its Application to Signature Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: Mathematical morphology has a rigorous theoretical basis and concise ideas. It is widely applicable to various aspects of image processing. Edge detection plays a vital role in image analysis, and binary morphology offers a simple yet efficient approach to handling such tasks. This paper applies five different morphological edge detection operators to binary images. It uses Structural Similarity (SSIM), Edge Preservation Index (EPI) and edge pixel error rate to evaluate the experimental results and obtain the optimal morphological edge detection operator. Furthermore, the operator is applied to the signature recognition system. The results show that the operator can effectively extract the edges of the signature image and that the quantitative evaluation indicators used in this paper can be used for signature authenticity recognition, laying a solid foundation for future signature recognition research.

articleTitle: A Programmable Heterogeneous SoC for Industrial IGBT Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: This paper proposes a programmable heterogeneous System on Chip (SoC) designed to control industrial Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistors (IGBTs), addressing the growing demand for IGBT monitoring and control in the industrial sector. The design integrates a Microcontroller Unit (MCU) and an embedded FPGA (eFPGA) to enable high-performance real-time control and communication for IGBTs, while also supporting monitoring and prediction algorithms through MCU software programmability. The SoC features an open-source RISC-V instruction set architecture called Xuantie E906 as the MCU, along with an eFPGA that uses an island-type layout. The eFPGA contains 16x16 hardware programmable logic units, providing 2048 four-input Lookup Tables (LUTs). Fabricated using TSMC's 40nm low-power process technology, the chip is packaged in a QFN format. A series of tests validate the basic functions of the SoC chip and the performance of its control protection circuit, achieving a favorable balance in area, frequency, and power consumption. In conclusion, the programmable heterogeneous SoC effectively combines the software flexibility of the MCU with the hardware parallel processing capabilities of the eFPGA, meeting the real-time response and complex computation needs of industrial IGBT control.

articleTitle: Peak Evaluation for Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry Data Using Neural Network on Statistical Quality Metrics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: Peak picking is a crucial step in the data analysis workflow of Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (LCMS) in untargeted metabolomics. The process is challenging due to interference from background signals such as noise and matrix effects. To address this challenge, we first collected 5,447 ion peaks and manually scored them after alignment. Next, we calculated 12 quality metrics for each ion peak. Finally, we developed a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) model to perform regression analysis, as well as binary and ternary classification, making it adaptable to various application scenarios. The results demonstrate that the MLP-based peak evaluation method is effective in accurately predicting peak quality. Researchers can quickly initiate their work by setting just one or two score thresholds based on their specific needs. This approach retains the flexibility to handle different datasets without the need to adjust thresholds for each peak quality metric, representing a step towards more flexible and efficient peak picking.

articleTitle: Agile Design of a RISC-V Processor with Trigonometric Math Extensions Using SpinalHDL
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: The purpose of hardware agile design is to speed up chip prototype verification and shorten the design cycle. The key of it is higher hardware description level, more flexible design reuse and faster design iteration. This paper uses SpinalHDL to design a five-stage pipeline RISC-V processor and expands five trigonometric math instructions based on the CORDIC algorithm. Using SpinalHDL offers a shorter design cycle and better processor configurability. The resource of processor is evaluated on Xilinx Kintex-7 XC7K325T-2FFG900C and the precision of the extended instruction is evaluated. Compared with the unextended processor, the consumption of LUTs and Registers of the extended processor increases by 53.20% and 19.97% respectively. These functions achieve an average 382× speedup in execution cycles when implemented using extended instructions instead of the standard math library.

articleTitle: Research and Implementation of Fast Decomposition Method for Symmetric Indefinite Sparse Linear Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: The fast solution of symmetric indefinite sparse ma-trices is of great significance in the fields of scientific computing and engineering design. However, the traditional solution methods are limited by the sparsity and indeterminacy of these matrices and fail to fully utilize their symmetry, leading to a large amount of storage redundancy and invalid computation. To address the aforementioned problems, a new method is designed to first reorder the matrices using the Reverse Cuthill-McKee (RCM) algorithm to efficiently compress the bandwidth of the matrices, and then an improved circuit implementation of the Aasen decomposition algorithm is proposed to accelerate the solution of indeterminate sparse matrices. The parallelism of the algorithm is fully exploited by constructing the chunked column compression storage mechanism and dynamic configuration control rules. Experimental results show that the method proposed in this paper can significantly improve the computational efficiency and stability of solving symmetric indeterminate sparse matrices, especially in specific applications, achieving a performance improvement of about 30x.

articleTitle: Research on Pedestrian Fall Detection Based on YOLOv8n
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: To address the challenges of finding an ideal balance between computational redundancy, accuracy, parameter count, and computational complexity in existing pedestrian fall detection algorithms, this paper proposes a lightweight pedestrian fall detection algorithm based on YOLOv8n. Firstly, a DWR-DRB module is designed to enhance the capabilities of large-kernel convolutional layers, extending the receptive field from the higher layers of the network to extract features, thereby reducing computational load and improving model performance. Secondly, a Deformable Attention mechanism is introduced to adaptively adjust the attention mechanism to focus on critical regions of the image, thereby enhancing the model's ability to recognize and localize targets. Finally., a CA-HSFPN module is constructed to improve the expressiveness of feature maps, Substantially decreasing the number of parameters and the computational complexity of the model, achieving a lightweight model. Experiments conducted on the constructed dataset show that the improved algorithm achieves a 0.7% increase in mape@0.5 compared to the original model, with a significant reduction in parameter count and computational load, with parameters decreasing by 33.2% and computational load decreasing by 16%, while maintaining high detection accuracy.

articleTitle: A Lightweight and Reliable Sideband Interface for Die-to-Die
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: To satisfy the low-power, low-cost and reliability requirements of the industrial control and intellisense applications, a lightweight sideband interface as well as protocol applied in die-to-die interface is proposed. It utilizes a simplified Management Data Input/Output protocol that supports parameter exchange and event communication with only two pins and half-duplex communication. Moreover, the proposed interface not only allows die-to-die communication after powerup without initialization and setup but also does not depend on the main-band. Therefore, it can play the role of emergency channel to improve the reliability of Die-to-Die. According to the synthesized result, the both-side equivalent gate count is 2400, while the leakage power is 140.19nW.

articleTitle: AggrBoost: A Load-Balanced Computing Engine for Boosting Aggregation in GCN Accelerators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: The emergence of Graph Convolutional Network marks a significant breakthrough in machine learning techniques for non-Euclidean spaces. During the graph aggregation process, several challenges arise, including load imbalance, low data reuse rate, and high off-chip data traffic. This paper proposes a computing engine for aggregation phase in GCNs based on a multi-edge parallel aggregation strategy with source node partitioning. This work featuring local sharing of source node feature vectors through source node partitioning and an encoding method named CSB (Compressed Sparse Block), achieves efficient load balancing under high parallelism through the equitable distribution of edge streams. It addresses memory access conflicts during the feature update process of destination nodes by utilizing distributed storage of partial sums, and effectively eliminates the pipeline stalls within partitions by Index-Driven MAC (Multiply-Accumulate). The PE utilization can exceed 97% on several popular datasets, making it suitable for application in GCN hardware accelerators.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization of Path Planning based on WCNN and Channel Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: Conventional methods for robot motion control and path planning often lack the reactive and flexible characteristics found in natural systems. Inspired by the brain's navigation mechanism using place cells-neurons that cognitively represent specific environments-a multi-objective optimization model to enhance computational efficiency and accuracy in path planning based on the Width-extended Convolutional Neural Network (WCNN) and Channel Attention Mechanism(CAM) is presented. Specifically, the width-extended convolutional neural network is expanded to intensify feature extraction within convolutional layers, without increasing network depth, thereby capturing crucial path information. Subsequently, channel attention mechanism prioritizes significant path features and constraints to enhance planning precision and minimize errors. Experimental validation on large-scale path planning datasets demonstrates that the method surpasses state-of-the-art multi-objective optimization of path planning techniques by achieving an optimal balance between accuracy and adaptability in path planning.

articleTitle: Layered Identification of Two-Dimensional(2D) Material Flakes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: 2D material is considered as the key to crack the chip performance bottleneck. After preparing 2D material flakes and obtaining their micro-optical images, it is still necessary to rely on manually experience to discriminate the material layers, which is inefficient, high workload, and poor accurate. Therefore, a method based on semantic segmentation is proposed to automatically identify the number of layers of 2D materials in this paper. First, the dataset images are color corrected, then a semantic segmentation model is trained to segment the flakes in the image, and finally a pre-trained Gaussian mixture model is used to fine-tune the semantic segmentation results. The experimental results show that the segmentation IoU results can reach 54.28%, 74.80% and 57.70% for the 1–3 layers of WSe2 2D material and 65.4%, 83.15%, 79.23% and 62.21% for the 1–4 layers of graphene 2D material, which can satisfy the needs of the study.

articleTitle: A Gray-level Morphological Operation Method Based on the Umbra Notion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: Mathematical morphology as a nonlinear image processing theory has been used in various aspects of image processing. However, with the emergence of morphological networks and the increasing resolution of images, the demand for the speed of morphological image processing is increasing. In this paper, we propose an implementation method of binary operations for gray-level morphology based on the umbra notion. In this method, firstly, the gray-level image to be calculated and the structural element image are converted into the corresponding binary umbra image according to the umbra notion. Then, dilation, erosion, opening and closing operations are performed on the umbra of the structural element image and the image to be processed to obtain the corresponding umbra result image. Finally, the umbra result image is converted into its top surface based on the linkage of the binary image with the pixel value of the gray-level image to obtain the corresponding gray-level image dilation, erosion, opening and closing operational results. The experimental results on one-dimensional and two-dimensional images demonstrate the effectiveness of the method, which can lay a foundation for the fast calculation of gray-level morphological images.

articleTitle: Efficient CNN Deployment on FPGA: A Dual Strategy for Feature and Weight Storage Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: In the traditionallayer-by-layer computation model, the deployment of classic Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models on resource-constrained Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) platforms faces frequent off-chip memory access issues, resulting in significant inference delays. To address this challenge, this paper proposes two solutions targeting layers with larger feature sizes: a feature row cache pipeline streaming mechanism based on an inter-layer handshake strategy and an on-chip weight storage optimization scheme based on inter-layer fusion and intra-layer chunking. To validate the feasibility of these solutions, we implement hardware acceleration experiments for the YOLOv4-Tiny model (layers 1–12) on Xilinx XCZU19EG, and explored the potential application of the core idea presented in this paper for processing layers with a larger number of weight parameters.

articleTitle: A High-Energy Dual-CDAC Single-Capacitor Switching Strategy Applied to SAR ADC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: An ultra-low power dual-CDAC switching strategy applied in SAR ADC is proposed. This switching scheme adopts two sub-CDAC structures. The first CDAC switching adopts the CDAC selection mode, and the subsequent first conversion adopts the overall reference voltage switching to realize the maximum two-bit quantization without power consumption. The subsequent switch only involves the capacitance in a single position of a single CDAC, which is simpler to switch, and the capacitance ratio on each CDAC is reduced by using a dual CDAC. The total capacitance is reduced from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2^{N-1}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2^{N-2}$</tex>, and the use of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{cm}$</tex> as the intermediate reference voltage can achieve lower switching power consumption than the existing research literature, and the same unit capacitance under the premise of N-bit resolution requires less total CDAC capacitance, reducing the area overhead. Through numerical simulation analysis, The proposed switching structure is reduced by 97.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> and area of proposed CDAC structure is optimized by 75%, which compared with traditional CDAC switching.

articleTitle: MATLAB-Based Performance Verification of 2.4-GHz All-Digital Sub-Sampling PLL with −125 dBc/Hz In-Band Noise
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: This paper presents a MATLAB and Simulink model for a 2.4 GHz All-Digital Sub-Sampling Phase-Locked Loop (ADSSPLL) which could meet the strict demands of IoT equipment. The proposed ADSSPLL uses Sub-Sampling Phase Detectors (SSPD) to replace the high-resolution Time-to-Digital Converter (TDC) and avoid using the frequency divider which could greatly improve the in-band noise and reduce the loop complexity. MATLAB and Simulink tools are used to verify the circuit performance of ADSSPLL. With the reference frequency at 50 MHz, the In-Band Noise is measured to −125 dBc/Hz@1 MHz, and it achieves a Root-Mean-Square (RMS) output jitter of 347 fs.

articleTitle: Design of a Novel TRNG Based on MSFRO and STR Entropy Source
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: True random numbers are used as keys because of their unpredictability, and True Random Number Generator (TRNG) is also part of the encryption system. In this paper, a new TRNG is designed, which uses Multi-Stage Feedback Ring Oscillator (MSFRO) and Self-Timing Ring (STR) as the mixed entropy source of TRNG. Among them, MSFRO improves randomness by increasing the feedback loops in the oscillator and using output results to control the number of feedback loops as well as increasing the clock jitter range and sampling frequency. The entropy source is sampled by the clock after frequency division, and then the optimized von Neumann verifier and lfsr after metastable elimination, so as to eliminate the correlation of the data and improve the randomness. In addition, AES encryption algorithm is also added to promote the randomness of generating random numbers to improve security. The TRNG is implemented on a DE2-115 FPGA board, and the generated bitstream under a clock operating at 50MHz successfully pass the 15 items of the NIST SP800-22 test. The randomness and independence of the entropy source are verified, which highlights its great potential for hardware security and performance.

articleTitle: XAS Distortion Correction Algorithm of Illicit Drug by ResU-Net Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: The increasing use of illegal or recreational drugs has continually posed a threat to public health and safety. As a result, there is an urgent need for an effective technique to detect these substances, particularly in field settings for rapid on-site detection. X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (XAS) is a spectral technique employed to qualitatively or quantitatively analyze the differences in X-ray absorption among substances. Its brief detection time and high accuracy render it well-suited for on-site detection of illicit drugs. However, traditional XAS detection algorithms analyze the feature envelope on each channel in its entirety, neglecting the temporal information and physical structural characteristics on different photon energy channels. Earlier methods for XAS substance detection have not utilized deep learning methods to correct spectral distortions. Expanding on this context, this paper introduces a novel approach for the detection of illicit drugs using X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy, proposing a new deep learning method for substance identification and spectral correction within XAS. This paper details a Residual Network-based U-Net spectral correction model, ResU-Net, that corrects distorted spectral data via deep learning, and it compares this model with conventional alternatives. Empirical testing and comparative evaluation, utilizing real-world data and performance metrics, demonstrate that the proposed ResU-Net spectral correction model surpasses alternative methods.

articleTitle: Improved CycleGAN for Synthesis and Recognition of Face Photo Sketches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: Facial photo-sketch synthesis and recognition is used in law enforcement to find key suspects. Nevertheless, the extant methodologies predominantly concentrate on the modal dissimilarities between photographs and sketches, and thus fail to fully consider identity information and detail preservation in the recognition task, which limits the recognition accuracy of synthesized images. For the purpose to deal with these issues, this paper puts forward a proposal for an identity-aware and detail-enhanced recurrent generative adversarial network. In this method, we optimize the generated sketches and photographs to retain more identity information and texture details by introducing perception loss and detail loss. Furthermore, by utilizing an attention strategy to boost the Visual Geometry Group(VGG) model's performance, we strengthen the recognition network and raise the accuracy of face picture sketch recognition. Finally, we perform experiments on the CUHK Face Sketch(CUFS) and CUHK Face Sketch FERET(CUFSF) datasets, and the results of the experiments are evidence of the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: FFT Processor for 3D Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: 3D imaging technology has developed rapidly and been widely applied in recent years, and Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) is a key component of 3D imaging technology. With the increasing demand for 3D-FFT scale and speed, data storage planning is the guarantee for imaging speed in large point 3D-FFT. In 3D-FFT, computations are required along three axes, and when the scale is large, data must be stored off-chip. As a result, when computing along the third axis, we will face the problem of crossing address access to stored data, significantly reducing 3D-FFT efficiency. The traditional method requires a total of six memory access operations, reading and writing along the X, Y, and Z axes individually, which ultimately fails to meet the bandwidth requirements. This paper proposes a 3D data storage scheme and address mapping strategy specifically for 3D-FFT data, along with a method to improve DDR data efficiency. These innovations reduce the number of memory accesses and improve the efficiency of memory access during cross-row addressing. To meet high throughput demands, a 16-parallel 256-point FFT structure and a 16-parallel transposition method are designed, improving the overall system performance from 60.902 ms with traditional methods to 33 ms, thereby meeting the 30 FPS performance requirement.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a NTT Accelerator Based on RISC-V for PQC Kyber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: RISC-V, as a new generation open-source Reduced Instruction Set Computing (RISC) architecture, has the advantages of low power consumption, small footprint, and high performance. Especially, RISC-V processors realized based on FPGA can be applied in different fields such as embedded systems, Artificial Intelligence (AI) chips, security devices and high-performance computing. It is foreseeable that a breakthrough in quantum computers will jeopardize all communications. Therefore, processors must integrate secure quantum computer anti-encryption techniques. Currently, the security and reliability aspects of processor implementations are still greatly underexplored. To address this gap, we propose three contributions. First, we augment the open-source IP Hummingbird E203 with a hardware module for implementing the Number-Theoretic Transform (NTT) operations of the Post-Quantum Cryptography (kyber). Second, we employ the hardware/software co-design techniques to accelerate NTT operations. Third, analyze the results of implementation. Prototyping was performed on FPGA to evaluate our designed processor NTT extension instructions. The cycle count for NTT operations is reduced by 84.55% and the instruction count is reduced by 81.25%. Enhanced computational efficiency applicable to information security systems under potential quantum computing threats is shown. The scalability of Post-Quantum Cryptography (kyber) based on riscv is realized.

articleTitle: A High-Output-Swing and Low-Current-Mismatch Charge Pump for PLL
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: This paper introduces a charge pump with high output swing and low current mismatch for Phase-Locked Loop (PLL). By effectively addressing the channel length modulation effect and charge sharing effect through the use of rail-to-rail operational amplifier structures with single-stage and two-stage input configurations, the charging and discharging currents of the charge pump are perfectly matched. Under the TSMC 40nm process, the charge pump's current range is from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{200}\boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{A}$</tex> to 3.8mA, and it can operate normally under a high-speed switching signal of 100MHz. With a supply voltage of 1.2V, the charge pump achieves a high output swing of 0.2V to 1.0V and a current mismatch of less than 0.022% across the entire current range.

articleTitle: Power Analysis on Hardware Implementation of CRYSTALS-Kyber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: CRYSTALS-Kyber is a post-quantum cryptography that can effectively resist quantum attacks. It has been included in the draft standard by NIST. Therefore, it is greatly important to research the side-channel security of its hardware implementation. In this paper, we propose an optimized chosen-ciphertext power analysis method for the hardware implementation of the CRYSTALS-Kyber. We conducted the side-channel security analysis experiments using the CW305 Artix-7 FPGA and analyzed the experimental results. The results demonstrate that our method can effectively exploit the side-channel leakage information from the hardware implementation of CRYSTALS-Kyber, improving the accuracy of the attack, reducing the number of power traces required, and achieving a key recovery accuracy of 98.8%.

articleTitle: An Analog Neural Computing Unit Circuit Design with $2\times 2$ MAC Based on CMOS for Storage-Computing Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: This paper presents a Neural Computing Unit (NCU) design with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> analog multiplier accumulation circuit which can achieve convolution and pooling operations for DNN algorithm. It has the function of integrating data storage and computation, which greatly improves energy efficiency of the chip for artificial intelligence processors. Using 180-nm CMOS process technology, an analog neural computing unit circuit has been designed in Cadence, including a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> multiplier accumulation circuit, digital to analog convertors, and voltage-to-time converters. Simulation results verify the convolution operation function. Meanwhile, storage-computing integration is also realized by this circuit. The performances of the designed NCU have also been evaluated and analyzed. The error of computing is within 5% on different corners and temperatures.

articleTitle: Optimization of the Book Recommendation System Based on Collaborative Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: A book recommendation system is a software system that uses computer technology and algorithms to recommend books that readers may be interested in. The system can identify readers' preferences and needs by analyzing data on their reading history, preferences and behaviors, and recommend related books. This system can help readers find the books that they are interested in faster and more accurately, improve the reading experience and efficiency, and can also help libraries or online bookstores to increase book borrowing or sales. At present, the book recommendation system is mainly divided into content-based recommendation system and collaborative filtering recommendation system. The content-based recommendation system recommends similar books by analyzing the attributes, themes and content characteristics of books. The collaborative filtering recommendation system recommends books to readers by comparing their behavior and preferences. It should be noted that there are some potential problems in the book recommendation system based on collaborative filtering, such as cold start problems, and data sparsity problems etc. To solve these problems, the hybrid recommendation algorithm, content-based recommendation, and other methods can be improved.

articleTitle: An Improved Dense Crowd Detection Model Based on YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: With the increase of crowd monitoring and management needs, dense crowd detection has become an important research direction in the field of computer vision, mainly using target detection methods to detect the position and number of pedestrians in pictures and videos. Aiming at the problem of missed detection and misdetection due to the occlusion between pedestrians or the target pedestrians being too small in dense crowd scenes, this paper proposes an improved detection algorithm CscSCA-YOLOv8 based on YOLOv8. Firstly, the Conv-SPD-Conv module is used instead of each convolutional step and each pooling layer in the trunk and the neck, to prevent the loss of fine-grained information and the less efficient feature representation Learning. Then the SCAMix hybrid attention mechanism is introduced into the YOLOv8 network architecture to utilize the global perception capability of self-attention and capture local features via CoordAttention to improve detection in dense scenes. Experimental results show that this paper's method achieves 74.1% and 46.6% for mAP50 and mAP50-95 on the WiderPerson dataset, respectively, and improves 3.6% and 2.8% compared with the original YOLOv8n.

articleTitle: Multi-Feature Fusion Classification Approach for Specific Communication Emitter Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: Addressing issues such as the limited focus on features and poor interpretability in deep learning models for the individual recognition of communication emitters, this study introduces a multi-domain feature fusion model. Initially, wavelet transforms are applied to raw signals to generate two-dimensional time-frequency images. Subsequently, features are extracted from these images using neural networks to form one-dimensional image feature vectors. Additionally, multi-domain parameters of the signals are manually extracted. These two types of feature vectors are concatenated to create a combined feature set. Simulation results indicate that, on the dataset of Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) emitters from multiple aircraft, selecting 10 categories of radiation sources, the proposed method improves identification accuracy by approximately 15% compared to using image features alone, achieving up to 97%. This enhancement significantly improves the accuracy of individual communication transmitter identification.

articleTitle: High-Speed Network Flow Classification: A Study and Design Based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: Network packet flow classification is the fundamental method for managing the security of network packets and is extensively applied within network security management systems, including network security isolation, intrusion protection, and security encryption. With the exponential growth of digital information in recent years, the rate of new-generation network communications has progressively escalated from the traditional 10 / 100 / 1000 M to the ultra-high-speed 10G / 40G / 100G. The ultra-high-speed network communication rate also brings new challenges to the performance of network data stream classification. This paper investigates four traditional mainstream network flow classification methods: rule tree matching, Ternary Content Addressable Memory (TCAM) matching, Hash table matching and direct comparison matching. A thorough analysis of the strengths and weaknesses of each method is presented. Given the absence of a method capable of dynamically updating the rule base, while simultaneously achieving full fuzzy matching of a high- speed, extensive rule base, this paper introduces a novel highspeed network flow classification approach using FieldProgrammable Gate Array (FPGA) technology. This method uses BRAM to build a rule array, calls DSP48E1 hard core and LUT resources in FPGA in a resource-balanced way to build a comparator, rearranges and splices the network data flow, and then matches it in parallel. The method is verified on the XC7V690T chip of XILINX. The results show that when performing 1000 five-tuple rule matching of fully fuzzy network, this method can not only update the five-tuple rule set in real time, but also use only 55,745 LUTs 1600 DSPs and 400 BRAMs resources to achieve the processing performance of 153MPPS throughput and 125ns latency, exceeding the minimum packet linear matching rate of 100G network.

articleTitle: MH-CLR: A Self-Supervised Learning Strategy Based on Hard Sample Mining and Masked Autoencoders
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 18th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: The integration of Whole Slide Imaging (WSI) technology with artificial intelligence has significantly enhanced the analysis and application of histopathological slides. However, existing supervised learning methods for WSI analysis demand extensive time and effort to annotate high-resolution slide images. In contrast, Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) pretraining strategies, which do not depend on explicit data annotations, have emerged as a promising alternative. These SSL strategies are rapidly narrowing the performance gap with supervised learning methods. In this context, we introduce an SSL framework that dynamically adjusts the selection of negative samples during contrastive learning within the SimCLR process and incorporates masked autoencoders to reconstruct original images using latent representations and masked annotations. Notably, our approach outperforms common SSL methods in downstream classification tasks, validated through testing on the PathMNIST and our collected lung squamous carcinoma datasets.
